bottleneck: Chronic pain often persists after tissue heals, driven by central sensitization — the nervous system amplifying its own signals — but the molecular and circuit basis of this chronification is unclear. Pain is subjective and lacks any objective measure, so trials rely on self-report, drugs target peripheral mechanisms for what is increasingly a central problem, and the same intervention helps one patient while worsening another. Opioids filled the therapeutic void with catastrophic results precisely because medicine could not measure or explain the condition it was treating. Without biomarkers, pain medicine remains pre-scientific.
current_state: No objective pain biomarker exists; non-opioid options remain limited. Central sensitization is described clinically but not mechanistically understood at the circuit level.

title: Chronic pain's central mechanisms unmapped
why_it_blocks: Chronic pain disables more people than almost any condition, yet medicine cannot measure it or explain its persistence. The opioid crisis was the cost of treating blind — and the blindness continues.
